item.title: Bishop Onah mourns four UNN students, commends Ortuanya’s leadership
item.description: By Alumona Ukwueze NSUKKA —The Catholic Bishop of Nsukka Diocese, Most Rev. Prof. Godfrey Igwebuike Onah, has joined the University of Nigeria, Nsukka (UNN), community in mourning the death of four students following a tragic incident at an off-campus house party. Bishop Onah, who paid a condolence visit to the Vice-Chancellor, Prof. Simon Ortuanya, on Friday, expressed sympathy and solidarity with the university community over the incident. He commended Ortuanya for his prompt response, particularly his efforts to establish the circumstances surrounding the deaths and his assurance that a thorough investigation would be conducted to determine the actual cause of the tragedy. The cleric expressed admiration for the Vice-Chancellor’s handling of the incident, noting that similar leadership qualities should be demonstrated at other levels of governance in the country. He also praised the Vice-Chancellor for identifying with the families of the deceased students and ensuring that the surviving students received necessary medical attention. While consoling the university community, Bishop Onah urged students to heed the Vice-Chancellor’s advice, abide by the institution’s rules and regulations and make judicious use of the opportunity to acquire university education. He further advised them to conduct themselves responsibly and remain focused on their academic pursuits, which he described as their primary reason for being in the institution. The Vice-Chancellor had on Thursday declared a three-day mourning period in honour of the deceased students. Ortuanya also visited the surviving students in various hospitals where they are receiving treatment, assuring them of the university management’s commitment to supporting their medical care and recovery. The post Bishop Onah mourns four UNN students, commends Ortuanya’s leadership appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Insecurity: Forgive me for not visiting communities, Tinubu begs Plateau residents
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has appealed to residents of Plateau State to forgive him for not visiting communities affected by recurring attacks, particularly Angwan Rukuba in Jos North Local Government Area, following the March 29 killings. Tinubu made the appeal on Saturday during the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Jos, where he acknowledged the devastation caused by years of violence in the state. The president explained that his previous visit to Plateau was restricted to the airport, but insisted that he had seen the extent of the destruction and received reports on the situation from Governor Caleb Mutfwang. “When I last visited, the other time, I was limited to the airport; forgive me if you didn’t see me in the hinterland, but I saw the devastation,” Tinubu said. “I got the report from the governor; I saw the horror in the faces of our people. “At the end of the day, we are fighting together; it is now that we can rebuild, and I assure those displaced that we will rebuild your communities, and we will bring you back to your community.” Tinubu, who acknowledged that attacks in Plateau since 2001 had claimed lives, destroyed homes and displaced communities, assured affected residents that his administration would support efforts to rebuild their communities and facilitate the return of displaced persons. He also urged residents to embrace peaceful coexistence, saying differences in language and other identities should not divide them. “Living in different rooms and speaking different languages does not make us enemies of one another. We have to live together, we have to farm together, we have to build this Plateau and this country together,” he said. The president also expressed condolences to families who lost loved ones, survivors of the attacks and residents whose homes were destroyed or who remained unable to return to their communities. “To every bereaved family, every home destroyed, every survivor, and everyone unable to return home, I offer my heartfelt condolences for your loss,” he said. On March 29, several residents of Angwan Rukuba were killed when unidentified gunmen opened fire on people at a popular bar in the community. The attackers were suspected to be cultists. Following the incident, Tinubu, during a visit to Jos in April, ordered the deployment of 5,000 artificial intelligence-enabled surveillance cameras to strengthen security in Plateau State. During the visit, he sympathised with the victims’ families, saying no amount of compensation could make up for their losses. He also met with stakeholders and some victims at the Plateau airport. However, his failure to visit the affected communities during that trip attracted criticism from Nigerians, some of whom questioned his decision to restrict his visit to the airport. item.title: Police arrest suspected terrorism financiers, bandits’ motorcycle suppliers
item.description: By: Kingsley Omonobi The Police Force Intelligence Response Team (IRT) has arrested suspected terrorism financiers, alleged motorcycle suppliers to bandits, armed robbery suspects and suspected kidnappers in separate intelligence-led operations across Kaduna and Plateau states. The operations also led to the recovery of five firearms, comprising two pistols and three locally fabricated pistols, as well as a motorcycle and a stolen Toyota Corolla. The Force Intelligence Department disclosed this during a briefing on the operational achievements of the IRT in Abuja, saying the operations formed part of sustained efforts to dismantle criminal networks involved in kidnapping, banditry, armed robbery and terrorism-related activities. Speaking at the briefing, IRT Commander, Deputy Commissioner of Police Adamu Muazu, said two suspects, identified as Nura Umar, 20, from Kidandan, and Alhaji Rabiu Aliyu, 58, from Zaria, Kaduna State, were arrested over alleged involvement in kidnapping and banditry-related activities. According to him, the suspects were arrested on August 29, 2026, following intelligence linking them to the supply of motorcycles to bandits operating in Kaduna and Katsina states. The police said the suspects allegedly confessed to supplying several motorcycles to bandit groups in the two states. One Honda CV-125 motorcycle without a registration number was recovered during the operation. The police described the arrests as significant to efforts to dismantle the financial and logistical networks sustaining kidnapping and banditry, adding that investigations were ongoing to identify other accomplices and trace the financial channels supporting the alleged activities. In another operation, the IRT arrested three suspected members of a criminal gang allegedly involved in one-chance operations, car snatching and armed robbery in Kaduna and its environs. The suspects were identified as Abdullahi Abubakar, Yusuf Mohammed and Bala Ibrahim. Abubakar was arrested on October 12, 2026, at about 8:30pm, following intelligence linking him to a gang allegedly targeting residents, particularly commercial tricycle and motorcycle operators. The police alleged that members of the gang strangled their victims before dispossessing them of their valuables. According to the police, Abubakar, who had previously served a 13-year jail term for a similar offence, identified a suspected gang leader, Boniface, said to be currently in Kaduna Prison. The police alleged that Boniface directed Abubakar to a hideout where the gang’s operational firearms were kept. Following the execution of a reproduction warrant, operatives recovered two pistols from the location. Further investigations reportedly led to the arrest of Mohammed and Ibrahim, who were identified as alleged receivers of stolen vehicles, motorcycles and tricycles. item.title: Navy uncovers 56,800 litres of stolen crude in Rivers
item.description: By: Kingsley Omonobi The Nigerian Navy has deactivated two illegal refining sites and uncovered approximately 56,800 litres of suspected stolen crude oil in Ogbogolo community, Ahoada West Local Government Area of Rivers State. The operation, conducted on November 13, 2026, was carried out by personnel of Nigerian Navy Ship (NNS) Soroh, a unit under Operation Delta Sentinel, following credible intelligence on illegal refining activities in the Orashi Forest. Director of Information, Navy Captain Abiodun Folorunsho, disclosed this in a statement, saying the operation uncovered two illegal refining sites containing one refining oven, 22 dugout pits and four sacks of suspected stolen crude oil. According to him, the first site contained approximately 1,800 litres of crude oil, while the second held an estimated 55,000 litres. He said the recovered products and associated items were subsequently handled in accordance with established anti-crude oil theft procedures. Folorunsho said the operation underscored the Nigerian Navy’s commitment to dismantling illegal refining infrastructure and disrupting networks involved in crude oil theft. He added that the Navy would continue to deploy intelligence-driven operations to deny oil thieves access to the nation’s petroleum resources and protect critical oil and gas infrastructure. The Navy, he said, remained committed to sustaining operational pressure on crude oil thieves and illegal refiners in support of national crude oil production, economic security and the protection of Nigeria’s maritime interests. item.title: [VIDEO] Taraba Records 72 Road Crash Deaths In 10 Months – FRSC
item.description: No fewer than 72 people died in 115 road traffic crashes recorded in Taraba State between January and October 2026, the Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) has said. The FRSC Sector Commander in Taraba, Anna Attah, disclosed this during a press briefing in Jalingo to mark the 2026 World Day of Remembrance for Road Traffic Victims. She said 374 people sustained injuries in the crashes, identifying excessive speeding and dangerous driving as major causes. Attah also said Nigeria recorded 7,156 road crashes, 3,445 deaths and 22,292 injuries between January and September 2026. item.title: 2027: Umo Eno backs Wike’s Rainbow Coalition for Tinubu
item.description: Akwa Ibom State Governor, Umo Eno, has declared support for the Rainbow Coalition led by the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, to mobilise support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027. Eno said he was willing to join any political coalition whose central objective was to secure Tinubu’s return to office in the 2027 presidential election. Speaking during a media chat on Saturday, the governor said he had thrown his weight behind the Rainbow Coalition, describing it as a platform for supporting the president. “That Rainbow Coalition is simply saying that we support President Tinubu as the president,” Eno said. He added: “If I will join and be a member of any coalition — whether it is Rainbow, call it any name. Any coalition that the central point is supporting the re-election of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu; I am for it.” The governor also said the relationship between the All Progressives Congress (APC) and the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Akwa Ibom State remained cordial, noting that both parties had reached an understanding on their political direction ahead of the 2027 elections. According to him, the arrangement involves supporting Tinubu, Senate President Godswill Akpabio and himself in the forthcoming elections. “I will work with all of them, and I think we are good on the ground in Akwa Ibom when it comes to the PDP-APC relationship,” he said. “We have agreed on the fact that we are supporting the president, we are supporting the Senate President, we are supporting the governor, and we have our clear understanding about those things.” BACK STORY The Rainbow Coalition, a cross-party political movement associated with Wike, has generated differing reactions within the APC, particularly over its implications for the party’s structures and candidates ahead of the 2027 general election. In September, APC leaders in the South-East backed the Progressive Governors’ Forum (PGF) in insisting that all party candidates should receive support in the 2027 elections. The leaders also rejected what they described as the “Rainbow (chameleon) Coalition”, warning that the party would resist any attempt to undermine its structures in the region. Their position followed the PGF’s declaration that it would not support any alliance or political arrangement capable of undermining Tinubu’s re-election bid or the electoral prospects of APC candidates. The governors were reportedly referring to the Rainbow Coalition, which Wike, a PDP member, has been promoting as a cross-party platform. In January, Wike said the coalition represented a departure from conventional party politics towards a collective political movement focused on advancing the interests of the state. item.title: 2027: ADC will defeat Tinubu in 13 Northern states – Amaechi
item.description: Rotimi Amaechi, the vice-presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), has expressed confidence that the party will defeat President Bola Tinubu in all 13 states of the North-East and North-West in the 2027 general election. Amaechi also predicted that the ADC would make significant inroads into the South-South and North-Central regions, specifically naming Niger, Kogi and Nasarawa states as territories the party expects to win. He spoke on Saturday at the ADC presidential campaign rally in Bauchi, where he warned that the party would not accept what he alleged was a repeat of the electoral events of the 2023 general election. “Because these people will do what they did in 2023. This time, we shall not agree. Do you understand? We will not do what?” he said. The former Minister of Transportation said the ADC had a stronger political presence across the North-East and North-West, which comprise 13 states. “We are the only party that comes with 13 states. The whole of North-East, the whole of North-West, that is 13, right? Let the president tell us how many states he comes with. He comes with only five in the South-West,” he said. Amaechi further predicted that the APC would lose another state in the South-West to the Allied Peoples Movement (APM). “That’s if he will. And the sixth state in the South-West will vote APM, whether he likes it or not,” he added. He said the ADC would challenge the APC in the South-South and North-Central, expressing confidence that the party would win Niger, Kogi and Nasarawa states. “We will fight with him in South-South. We will fight with him in North-Central. And be sure, be rest assured, Niger, Kogi, Nasarawa will be in ours easily,” he said. On the South-East, Amaechi dismissed the prospect of Tinubu making significant electoral gains in the region, insisting that the ADC would emerge victorious. “He will not go to South-East at all. Be rest assured, we will win. We will win. Things will get better,” he said. The post 2027: ADC will defeat Tinubu in 13 Northern states – Amaechi appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Tinubu has performed credibly in North, deserves second term – Bichi
item.description: The Chairman, House Committee on Appropriations, Rep. Abubakar Bichi, says President Bola Tinubu has performed credibly in Northern Nigeria. Bichi, who stated this in an interview with the News Agency of Nigeria in Dutse, Jigawa, insisted that the region had benefited significantly from Tinubu administration’s policies and development projects. He described the growing support for Tinubu’s reelection in the North as impressive. He said the turnout of people from the North at the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential campaign rallies was a clear indication of their satisfaction with the achievements of Tinubu. “Contrary to claims in some quarters that Tinubu does not care about the North. “The president has demonstrated commitment to the development of the region through major infrastructure and other intervention projects. “The turnout of people from the north is impressive, and it is a clear testimony that the people are happy with what Tinubu has done so far. “President Bola Tinubu has performed credibly in the North, and there is no state that has been left out,” Bichi said. He cited Jigawa as an example, explaining that the president had approved about N80 billion for the Greater Dutse Water Project to address one of the state’s major developmental challenges. He also highlighted ongoing and completed road projects in the state, particularly the Kano-Hadejia road, which he said, covered approximately 200 kilometres. According to him, the section from Kano to Danja has been completed, while work on the Danja-Hadejia stretch has reached about 80 per cent completion. Bichi further said that several irrigation projects had also been completed in Jigawa. He noted that such interventions demonstrated the federal government’s commitment to improving infrastructure and agricultural development in the region. “As Chairman of the House Committee on Appropriations, I know what President Tinubu has done in many parts of the North, and it is fantastic,” he said. Bichi dismissed suggestions that the president was indifferent to the welfare of Northern Nigerians. The lawmaker maintained that Tinubu administration had recorded significant achievements across the North-West and other parts of the region. “Some people are saying what they want to say, that President Tinubu doesn’t care about the north and doesn’t like our people, but it is not true. “I know what he has done here, I know what he has done in the North-West, and he has done extremely well,” he said. Bichi specifically mentioned Kano, Jigawa, Katsina, Sokoto, Kebbi and Zamfara among the states that had benefited from the President’s development initiatives. He expressed confidence that the people of Kano would demonstrate their appreciation for the president’s contributions. He added that he would provide further details of the projects executed in the state. item.title: Ajaero recalls 30-year bond as NLC scribe Ugboaja goes home
item.description: By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — President of the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC), Comrade Joe Ajaero, has paid an emotional tribute to the late National Secretary of the Congress, Comrade Emmanuel Ugboaja, describing him as more than a brother and recalling their 30-year relationship built on friendship, shared struggles and comradeship. Ajaero spoke on Saturday at Ugboaja’s burial in his Nkpa community, Abia State, where he said the depth of their personal relationship made him feel he was not the right person to deliver a tribute to the deceased. “Ugboaja was not just a friend. I don’t know how else to describe him. He was more than a brother. We shared the same fate. We are brothers in Christ and comrades in this family. We shared secrets. I found in him part of me,” he said. Describing the deceased as a perfect gentleman and one of the finest personalities in the labour movement, Ajaero said Ugboaja was dependable, courageous and committed to the interests of ordinary Nigerians, despite his connections with influential people. According to him, the late labour leader maintained relationships with successive presidents and presidential committees without allowing such connections to compromise his solidarity with the masses. “He knows the high and the mighty, yet he tilts towards the masses. If you have the most difficult assignment, give it to him to deliver. He doesn’t mince words in calling a spade a spade,” Ajaero said. He recalled that Ugboaja remained committed to his responsibilities even during his prolonged illness, disclosing that he was still attending to pressing matters at the NLC office barely three days before his death. Ajaero expressed confidence that his departed friend had gone to rest in the bosom of the Lord. Speaking on behalf of the family, the deceased’s immediate younger brother, Patrick Ugboaja, described him as an exceptional individual whose life was defined by service, sacrifice and concern for humanity. He said the deceased was his role model and a dependable source of guidance, adding that following in his footsteps had not been easy. “I have always looked up to him for direction. He was one person who had an answer to almost everything. When this happened, I looked around and wondered what he would have advised me to do,” he said. Patrick said his brother fought for the rights of the oppressed and touched countless lives across communities and beyond Nigeria. He expressed gratitude to dignitaries, labour leaders, friends and sympathisers who travelled from different parts of the country to honour the late unionist. In his sermon, the officiating preacher urged Nigerians to live purposeful lives, stressing that death was inevitable irrespective of one’s position, wealth, academic qualifications or influence. He challenged political leaders, public office holders, professionals and ordinary citizens to build enduring legacies through justice, forgiveness, humility and service to humanity. item.title: 2027: Diri charges Bayelsa APC to deny opposition 25% votes
item.description: By Samuel Oyadongha, Yenagoa Governor Douye Diri of Bayelsa State has charged members of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in the state to intensify grassroots mobilisation to ensure that no opposition party secures 25 per cent of the votes in the 2027 presidential and National Assembly elections. Diri gave the charge at the grand finale of the Bayelsa East Renewed Hope Movement sensitisation campaign in Ogbia Town, where he urged party members to consolidate their political gains and reach out to undecided voters ahead of the elections. Represented by his deputy, Dr Peter Akpe, the governor said the APC could not afford to become complacent despite its political standing in the state, insisting that members must sustain their mobilisation efforts to secure an overwhelming victory. He also commended political leaders and stakeholders in Bayelsa East for embracing reconciliation and sustaining peace, describing unity as essential to the political and developmental progress of the area. Speaking on behalf of the governor, Akpe said the party appreciated the sacrifices and commitment of its members, particularly those who attended the event despite the rain. He, however, warned that the mobilisation drive must continue, urging party leaders to bring undecided voters into the APC fold. “But saying thank you does not mean you should go to sleep. It is time to dot the i’s and cross the t’s. One or two people are out there waiting for us to harvest. Bring them inside. Do not leave them outside because we want to squeeze the opposition to zero point. “Our winning is sure, but if we score 75 per cent, we have not won because the other people should not get 25 per cent. I emphasise that no opposition party or candidate should get 25 per cent of votes in Bayelsa,” he said. In his remarks, the Managing Director of the Niger Delta Development Commission (NDDC), Dr Samuel Ogbuku, claimed that former President Goodluck Jonathan had endorsed President Bola Tinubu and all APC candidates ahead of the 2027 elections. Ogbuku said APC candidates from Bayelsa East had visited Jonathan to seek his permission and blessings before commencing their sensitisation campaign. He said the former president had endorsed the candidates and encouraged them to work towards victory in the forthcoming elections. “As a people who respect leadership, we first took all our candidates to see the former president of Nigeria, Dr Goodluck Ebele Jonathan, who is also from this electoral district, to seek his permission and his blessings. “In that meeting, the former president actually blessed this movement, blessed our candidates and endorsed all of them, from president to the least candidate, and gave us a mandate to go out to win the election for the senatorial district,” Ogbuku said. item.title: Atiku pledges Mambilla completion, end to unnecessary taxes if elected
item.description: BAUCHI — Presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar, has pledged to complete the long-abandoned Mambilla Hydropower Project in Taraba State if elected president in the 2027 general election. Atiku also promised to restore petrol subsidy, reintroduce electricity subsidy and abolish what he described as unnecessary taxes imposed on Nigerians. He made the pledges on Saturday at the ADC presidential campaign rally in Bauchi, where he urged residents of the North-East to support his party in the forthcoming election. The former Vice-President said the North-East was endowed with enormous mineral resources, including crude oil, but successive administrations had failed to harness the region’s potential for the benefit of its people. “I promise you that, by God’s grace, if you vote for us, we will ensure this oil work is completed for the prosperity of the North-East,” he said in Hausa. Speaking on the Mambilla Hydropower Project, Atiku recalled that successive governments had made promises to execute the project without bringing it to completion. “For those of you who are older, you will recall that since the era of Sir Abubakar Tafawa Balewa, there have been promises to build a dam called the Mambilla Hydroelectric Power Project, which past governments failed to actualise. “If God gives us the opportunity, and ADC is voted into power along with me, I promise you that we will continue and complete that project,” he said. On taxation, the ADC candidate pledged that his administration would eliminate taxes he considered unnecessary and unjustified. He also promised to tackle insecurity and banditry in the North-East, warning that those responsible for criminal activities would not be allowed to operate with impunity under his administration. “Finally, we know that here in the North-East, we face insecurity issues and banditry. I swear, if the president were not somehow, nobody would dare to commit this nonsense under my watch and get away with it,” he said. Atiku urged residents to vote for the ADC in 2027 and protect their votes until they were officially recorded. The former Vice-President also thanked Bauchi State Governor, Bala Mohammed, for providing the party access to the stadium and government lodges for its campaign rally, despite the ADC being in the opposition. “The Bauchi State governor did not take things too far, he gave us the opportunity to campaign in this stadium and provided us with all the government lodges. For doing that, we thank him, even though we remain in the opposition,” he said. Mambilla project and contractual dispute The Mambilla Hydropower Project, located in Taraba State, was conceived in 1972 under the military administration of former Head of State, General Yakubu Gowon, but has remained uncompleted for decades. item.title: US Thrash Haiti As Pochettino Prepares For Farewell
item.description: The United States thrashed Haiti 6-0 to surge towards the CONCACAF Nations League semi-finals on Saturday as Mauricio Pochettino’s penultimate game in charge ended in an emphatic victory. Goals from Christian Pulisic (2), Auston Trusty, Julian Hall, Weston McKennie and Folarin Balogun gave the US a commanding first-leg advantage to all but settle the outcome of the quarter-final before Tuesday’s second leg in Cincinnati. The build-up to Saturday’s fixture in Miami had been overshadowed by news of Pochettino’s departure as US coach after agreeing to take over Manchester United. But there was little sign that news of Pochettino’s exit had disturbed US preparations as they demolished World Cup qualifiers Haiti to deliver the biggest victory of the Argentine coach’s two-year reign. “Pochettino is an amazing manager, and he’s added a lot to us with the national team,” goalscorer Balogun said afterwards. “It’s always sad when you see a top coach leave, but it’s a part of the sport. “I think it was just important for us today to stick together and get the win — it just makes the send-off better,” Balogun added. Trusty gave the Americans the lead after just 10 minutes, confidently finishing from close range after Sebastian Berhalter’s free-kick from the right flank. Fans of Haiti cheer during the CONCACAF Nations League Quarterfinal match between Haiti and United States at Nu Stadium on November 14, 2026 in Miami, Florida. JC Ruiz/Getty Images/AFP (Photo by JC Ruiz / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP) That goal was all that separated the teams at half-time, but the floodgates opened after the break. Hall calmly tucked away Antonee Robinson’s low cross in the 52nd minute after a sweeping counter-attack to make it 2-0. Pulisic made it 3-0 from the penalty spot 10 minutes later after being brought down in the box by Haiti defender Carlens Arcus. The AC Milan forward then grabbed his second goal a minute later, rifling into the bottom corner from the edge of the area to make it 4-0. McKennie’s 68th-minute header put Pochettino’s side 5-0 up, and the US thought they had added a sixth soon afterwards when Balogun shrugged off Arcus to score from close range. Weston McKennie #8 of United States celebrates scoring his team’s fifth goal during the CONCACAF Nations League Quarterfinal match between Haiti and United States at Nu Stadium on November 14, 2026 in Miami.(Photo by JC Ruiz / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP) A VAR review, however, determined that Balogun had fouled Arcus in the build-up and the goal was chalked off. Balogun did not have long to wait, though, for his 13th international goal, latching on to a Malik Tillman through ball to score in the 82nd minute. AFP The post US Thrash Haiti As Pochettino Prepares For Farewell appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Over 40 killed as vigilantes clash with bandits in Zamfara
item.description: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo More than 40 people, including suspected bandits and local vigilantes, have reportedly been killed in a gun battle between armed men and local security volunteers in Zoma community, Bukkuyum Local Government Area of Zamfara State. Among the suspected bandits reportedly killed in the confrontation was a notorious commander identified as Jiji. The incident occurred last Wednesday when the armed men allegedly attacked the community, prompting local vigilantes to mobilise and confront them. According to a report by the BBC Hausa Service monitored by our correspondent, a resident of Zoma, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said the vigilantes were alerted by telephone shortly after the attackers arrived. He said residents also contacted neighbouring communities, urging them to mobilise and support the fight against the attackers. However, he alleged that an informant leaked information about their mobilisation to the bandits before the confrontation escalated. “The clash lasted from about 8:30 a.m. until 12 noon. Our people killed many of the gunmen, but they also killed nine of our men. Among the bandits killed was one of their commanders known as Jiji,” the resident said. Describing the incident as painful despite what he considered a successful resistance, the resident lamented the loss of several young men from the community. “We don’t have any help except from Allah. All we are asking for is assistance and weapons. If they provide us with arms, they should leave us to confront the gunmen,” he added. Another resident, who also spoke to the BBC Hausa Service, said the attackers approached from the eastern part of Zoma and had previously terrorised neighbouring communities. He added that those killed in the confrontation were buried on Wednesday. Meanwhile, reports indicated that suspected bandits operating in the Dansadau area of Zamfara State had resorted to imposing levies on residents of communities under their control. The police had yet to issue an official statement on the reported clash and casualty figures as of the time of filing this report. On transportation infrastructure, the governor identified the Akwanga-Jos-Bauchi-Gombe-Biu road corridor and the proposed railway development from Jos towards the North-East as projects expected to improve connectivity and economic activities in the region. He also highlighted the Ultramodern International Livestock Market, International Grains Market, Timberland Abattoir and Inland Dry Port as initiatives aimed at strengthening Gombe’s commercial activities, attracting investment and creating employment opportunities. The governor said his administration had constructed more than 1,100 kilometres of roads across the state, adding that the APC was seeking the electorate’s support based on its record in office. “We are not promising; we are asking you to rate us based on our deliverables. item.title: Nwifuru is silently taking Ebonyi to greater heights, and touching every sector
item.description: By Anayo Okoli The trending is narrative given to the public in and outside Ebonyi State by opposition is that Governor Francis Nwifuru is not working. And this narrative has gained currency among the people. But a visit to the state indicates that indeed the contrary is the case. The Governor is indeed doing working and touching every sector of development. The reality on ground is that a lot of development is happening in the State. Across the 13 local government areas of thespian state, no community is left out, at least with a road project. According to records, on assumption of office, Governor Francis Nwifuru unfolded what he called “People’s Charter of Needs” as a priority guide to his development trajectory and his administration has followed this religiously. In fact some of the ongoing projects are landmark projects that would project the state to national and even international maps. For instance, two specialized universities being built by the government will change the education landscape of the State. One of them, the ICT University has taken off at a temporary site with over 100 students receiving education free of charge. Work at the permanent site in Oferekpe, located in a vast land space, is ongoing with many sections, including lecturers quarters, classroom blocks, Senate building, student hostels almost completed. Construction of a teaching hospital is also going at ICT University. There is also the Aeronautical University located not far from the Chuba Okadigbo airport. Government sources said that the National University Commission has accredited the University to take off next academic session. The university will train engineers of various specialties. Indeed, a lot of structures are springing up at the massive sites in an effort to be ready for the take off of academic activities. From what is on ground, Nwifuru is investing a lot in the education sector and manpower development. He has awarded full Masters and PhD scholarship sponsorship to 1,400 Ebonyi indigenous students to universities in the United Kingdom and Nigeria; renovated some structures at State University and raised its subvention from N150 million to N280 million as well as released N700 outstanding subvention to the institutions. He also extended the good gesture to the State College of Education, Ikwo, which he upgraded to a University of Education. Many dilapidated primary and secondary schools have been rehabilitated. About 2000 primary and secondary school teachers were recruited. These are some of the governor’s major undertakings in the education sector. In the health sector, the administration has also recorded a lot of progress. In its determination to change the narrative and make the residents of the State have access to quality healthcare, the government embarked on massive recruitment of healthcare workers. 653 medical personnel were employed across Ebonyi State, including doctors and other medical personnel. item.title: Meet 2 African countries to ever break into top five FIFA World Ranking
item.description: Only two African countries have ever reached the top five of the FIFA Men’s World Ranking, with Nigeria and Morocco achieving the historic feat more than three decades apart. The Super Eagles of Nigeria were the first African team to break into the world’s top five, reaching fifth place in April 1994. The achievement came during one of the most memorable periods in Nigerian football history, following the country’s victory at the 1994 Africa Cup of Nations in Tunisia. Nigeria, coached by Clemens Westerhof, had a talented generation featuring Rashidi Yekini, Daniel Amokachi, Emmanuel Amunike, Finidi George, Sunday Oliseh and Austin Jay-Jay Okocha. The Super Eagles also made their debut at the 1994 FIFA World Cup in the United States, where they topped their group before being eliminated by Italy in the round of 16. For 32 years, Nigeria’s fifth-place ranking remained the highest position ever achieved by an African national team. However, Morocco joined the exclusive list in September 2026 after climbing to fifth in the FIFA Men’s World Ranking. The Atlas Lions’ rise followed a period of impressive performances, including their historic run to the quarter-finals of the 2026 FIFA World Cup. Morocco had also made history at the 2022 World Cup in Qatar, becoming the first African country to reach the semi-finals of the competition. Their latest achievement saw them equal Nigeria’s record, making them the second African country to reach fifth place in the global ranking. According to FIFA, Morocco’s achievement matched the highest position ever attained by an African national team, a record Nigeria had held since April 1994. The two African countries are: Nigeria: Fifth place in April 1994. Morocco: Fifth place in September 2026. The two countries have therefore written their names into African football history, becoming the only representatives of the continent to reach the top five of the FIFA Men’s World Ranking. item.title: CHINA DIARIES: The Future of farming
item.description: When we talk about China’s development, the images that often come to mind are high-speed trains, towering skyscrapers, electric vehicles and impressive infrastructure. But there is another quiet revolution taking place, one that is just as important to China’s future: agriculture. I had an opportunity to explore this during a visit to Yangling, in Shaanxi Province, a place that has become an important centre for agricultural science, research, innovation and technology. Our visit took us to three facilities: the SCO Demonstration Base for Agricultural Technology Exchange and Training, the Yangling Smart Agriculture Demonstration Park, and Yangling Liangke Agricultural Science and Technology Co. Ltd. What I saw offered an interesting glimpse into how China is using science and technology to rethink farming, improve productivity and strengthen food security. China Diaries: An Emperor, 8,000 Soldiers and a Lesson for Nigeria! 2027: We’ll fight Tinubu in South, North-Central, sweep North-West, North-East – Amaechi And, naturally, it got me thinking about Nigeria. Where farming meets the digital age One of the most interesting parts of the visit was seeing how technology is being integrated into everyday agricultural activities. At the smart agriculture demonstration facility, I saw a control station where plants are monitored through screens. Rather than relying entirely on physical observation, information about growing conditions can be monitored centrally, allowing operators to keep track of what is happening inside the growing facilities. It was a reminder that modern farming is increasingly becoming a data-driven activity. The farmer of the future may still walk through the farm, inspect the crops and get his hands dirty, but technology is giving him additional tools to make better decisions. I also saw vegetables being cultivated indoors in a controlled environment. It was fascinating to see food production taking place in a setting that looked quite different from the conventional farms we are familiar with in Nigeria. The idea is to manage growing conditions and create a more controlled environment for production. Such systems can help reduce dependence on some external weather conditions and make production more predictable, although their commercial viability depends on energy, infrastructure and operating costs. Another interesting sight was the display of grains and seedlings. These may look ordinary at first glance, but they represent an important part of the agricultural value chain: research, seed development and the effort to improve the quality and productivity of crops before they even get to the farm.
